sections.title: Basic Concept of Mirror Image
sections.content:
In a Mirror Image, the object is reversed left to right. The left side becomes right and the right side becomes left. The top and bottom remain the same.

2–3 Step Method:
1. Identify the left and right parts of the figure.
2. Swap left with right.
3. Keep top and bottom unchanged.

sections.title: Basic Concept of Water Image
sections.content:
In a Water Image, the object is reversed top to bottom. The upper part becomes lower and the lower part becomes upper. The left and right remain the same.

2–3 Step Method:
1. Identify the top and bottom parts.
2. Swap top with bottom.
3. Keep left and right unchanged.

sections.title: Mirror Image of Clocks
sections.content:
To find the mirror image time of a clock, use the 11:60 subtraction rule.

Rule: Mirror Time = 11:60 - Given Time

Example: If the time is 4:15
Step 1: Subtract 4:15 from 11:60.
Step 2: 11:60 - 4:15 = 7:45
Step 3: The mirror image time is 7:45.

sections.title: Alphabet Symmetry
sections.content:
Some capital letters look the same in a mirror because they are vertically symmetrical. Examples: A, H, I, M, O, T, U, V, W, X, Y.

2–3 Step Method:
1. Imagine a vertical line in the middle of the letter.
2. Check if both halves are identical.
3. If yes, the letter is mirror symmetrical.

sections.title: Basic Word Reflection
sections.content:
In a Mirror Image, a word appears in reverse order.

Example: APPLE
Step 1: Write the letters in reverse order.
Step 2: E L P P A
Step 3: This is the mirror image.

In a Water Image, the order remains the same but letters appear upside down.

sections.title: Directional Reflection
sections.content:
In a Mirror Image, East and West are interchanged, but North and South remain the same.

Example: If an arrow points North-East
Step 1: Replace East with West.
Step 2: Keep North unchanged.
Step 3: The mirror direction is North-West.

sections.title: Common Mistakes
sections.content:
1. Confusing Mirror Image with Water Image.
2. Using 12:00 instead of 11:60 in clock problems.
3. Changing North-South in Mirror Image questions.
4. Forgetting to reverse the word order in mirror questions.

sections.title: Quick Summary
sections.content: Mirror Image changes left and right. Water Image changes top and bottom. Use 11:60 rule for mirror clock problems. Always check direction swaps carefully and practice mental visualization.

tricks.title: 11:60 Clock Trick
tricks.explanation: For mirror time, subtract the given time from 11:60.

tricks.title: Exact Hour Shortcut
tricks.explanation: If the time is exactly on the hour, subtract the hour from 12.

tricks.title: East-West Swap Rule
tricks.explanation: In mirror image, only East and West change.

tricks.title: Top-Bottom Water Rule
tricks.explanation: In water image, only top and bottom change.

tricks.title: Reverse Word Trick
tricks.explanation: Write the word in reverse order for mirror image.

tricks.title: Vertical Symmetry Check
tricks.explanation: Draw a vertical line in the middle of the letter.
tricks.example: A is symmetrical, F is not.

tricks.title: Identical Number Trick
tricks.explanation: Some numbers like 0, 1, and 8 look the same in mirror.

tricks.title: Option Elimination Trick
tricks.explanation: Remove options that do not follow correct reversal rule.
tricks.example: If it is mirror image, eliminate same-order options.
